links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to breast cancer questions (Flesch Kincaid scale)
links.effect: Average readability was poor at 37.9 (range 18.0-60.5), with high concordance across repetitions (ICC 0.73).
links.quote: The average readability was poor at 37.9 (range, 18.0-60.5) with high concordance (ICC, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90; p < .001).

links.outcome: Validity of references cited by ChatGPT in responses
links.effect: Average 1.97 references per response (total 119); peer-reviewed articles cited only once; nonexistent websites in 41%.
links.quote: ChatGPT cited peer-reviewed articles only once and often referenced nonexistent websites (41%).

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT responses to patient breast cancer questions
links.effect: Average accuracy score 1.88 (4=worst); responses incorrect 24% of the time; clinical concordance 2.79.
links.quote: Because ChatGPT 3.5 responses were incorrect 24% of the time and did not provide real references 41% of the time, patients should be cautioned about using ChatGPT for medical information.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates ChatGPT 3.5's accuracy, clinical concordance, and readability on breast cancer questions without testing any specific guardrail or deployment practice.
